understanding.emotion: I'm looking for something deeper to lean on
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call searching for what it's all for, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.insight: Nothing is exactly wrong, and that's the hard part. You've outgrown the reasons that used to carry you.

situations.label: I want to reconnect with my roots
Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.
queries.act: Turn toward what lasts: serve, study, reflect daily, and offer your work to something beyond yourself.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

understanding.life_context: Working. Feels searching; closest to "My pet died" and "I want to reconnect with my roots".

plan_v3.first_line: You are grieving a deep loss, and your heart knows a pain no one else can fully understand.

hook.ref: Mahabharata · Udyoga Parva · Udyoga: Krishna's peace embassy
hook.speaker: Yudhishthira
hook.setting: Before Krishna leaves for the Kaurava court, Yudhishthira lays out why he wants peace, not war.
hook.sanskrit: अधनाद्धि निवर्तन्ते ज्ञातयः सुहृदो द्विजाः / अपुष्पादफलाद्वृक्षाद्यथा कृष्ण पतत्रिणः
hook.line: When money runs out, some friends drift away, like birds leaving a tree with no fruit.
hook.translation: When a man has no money, relatives, friends and brahmins turn away from him, the way birds leave a tree that has no flowers and no fruit.
hook.why: Winning a feud still costs you peace. Hostility only ends when someone stops feeding it.

prasang.title: Yudhishthira's case for peace
prasang.summary: Before Krishna sets out as peace envoy, Yudhishthira opens his heart: poverty humiliates, greed corrodes, victory breeds enmity, and hostility is never ended by hostility. He asks only for five villages.
prasang.lesson: Winning a feud still costs you peace. Hostility only ends when someone stops feeding it.

alternates.speaker: Vibhishan
alternates.setting: Vibhishan, Ravana's good-hearted brother, describes his life in Ravana's court.
alternates.sanskrit: सुनहु पवनसुत रहनि हमारी। जिमि दसनन्हि महुँ जीभ बिचारी॥ तात कबहुँ मोहि जानि अनाथा। करिहहिं कृपा भानुकुल नाथा ॥
alternates.line: I live here like the tongue among the teeth.
alternates.translation: Son of the wind, hear how I live: like the poor tongue among the teeth. Friend, knowing me to be without support, will the Lord of the Sun dynasty ever show me grace?
alternates.why: Even in a hostile place there may be one ally; find them.

prasang.title: Hanuman finds a friend in Lanka
prasang.summary: Searching Lanka, Hanuman is surprised to find a house with Ram's name on it. Its owner, Vibhishan, Ravana's brother, says he lives in Lanka like a tongue among teeth. Hanuman tells him even a restless monkey like himself was given Ram's love.
prasang.story_hook: In a city of demons, Hanuman heard someone wake up and say Ram's name.
prasang.lesson: Even in a hostile place there may be one ally; find them.
